identity.title: On Minimum Depth and Width of Floating-Point Neural Networks for Representing Floating-Point Functions

problem.claim: Determine the minimum depth and width needed for floating-point ReLU networks to represent every function from floating-point vectors to floating-point scalars.

gap.claim: Exact-arithmetic expressivity results cannot be directly applied to computer implementations using finite-precision numbers and inexact operations with round-off error.

contributions.claim: Characterizes minimum depth and width for representing all functions from \mathbb F^d to \mathbb F with floating-point ReLU networks.
Shows exact minimum depth three, and bounds the minimum width between 2d and 2d+4; for non-negative-float domains, the width lies between d and d+4.

stated_novelty.claim: The work analyzes expressivity directly in the floating-point setting, where prior cited results were derived under exact arithmetic.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that representing all functions on \mathbb F^d requires exactly three layers, although two layers may suffice for a smaller domain and/or codomain.
The authors report width bounds of 2d to 2d+4 for the full floating-point domain, narrowing to d to d+4 for non-negative floats; smaller domains can require still less width.
The authors report that exact-arithmetic results do not extend to the floating-point setup.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior expressivity work identified minimum depth and width for universal approximation and memorization.
Those results assume exact arithmetic, unlike finite-precision computer implementations with round-off errors.
The paper studies ReLU networks with floating-point parameters and operations, targeting all maps from \mathbb F^d to \mathbb F.
It reports exact depth three and width bounds, with reduced bounds for non-negative or smaller domains, and concludes that exact-arithmetic results do not carry over.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates the full-domain characterization from restricted-domain cases, reporting different depth and width bounds for smaller or non-negative domains.

lessons.interpretation: Expressivity claims can depend materially on arithmetic model and domain/codomain restrictions.
lessons.application: State the computational arithmetic model and domain restrictions alongside any expressivity bound, then report how the bound changes under meaningful restrictions.
lessons.exception: This framing is less useful when the work genuinely concerns idealized exact arithmetic or a fixed unrestricted domain.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the precise layer convention, width definition, floating-point format, or whether the bounds are tight beyond the stated depth result.
No proof details, constructions, datasets, empirical evaluations, or comparisons beyond the stated theoretical claims are provided.
